note: caseInsensitive where Java's simple case mappings differ from XPath's full ones: ß has no single-character upper case and stays ß (U+00DF), after SS (folded to ss); İ (U+0130) folds to i, so İ, I and i are equal and keep their input order. Input İ, SS, h, ß, I, i gives h, İ, I, i, SS, ß; full mappings would make ß equal to SS and put İ last. R1 joins the contexts S1 keeps, so All shows each context's order in turn. Observe in SAP PO (#33).
